filterExpression.description: Optional. Filters the events counted in the report by custom keys. Not all reports support this filter. It is currently only supported for web apps; see the report's `usage` field for whether `filter_expression` is supported. Requests for other apps or unsupported reports that set this field are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Supported forms: * Equality: `custom_keys.level = "vip"` * Has: `custom_keys.level:"vip"` (matches the same events as equality) * Presence: `custom_keys.level:*` * OR across values of one key: `custom_keys.level = "vip" OR custom_keys.level = "enterprise"` * AND across different keys: `custom_keys.level = "vip" AND custom_keys.region = "us"` Keys are case-sensitive. Keys and values containing spaces must be double-quoted, for example `custom_keys."app state" = "background"`. OR across different keys, repeating a key within an AND, NOT, and comparators other than `=` and `:` are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT. Wildcards are not supported in values; use `custom_keys.:*` to match events that set a key to any value. This filter expression applies in addition to the `filter` field above. The syntax is a subset of AIP-160 (https://google.aip.dev/160).

filter.issue.content.description: Optional. A space separated list of filter terms matched against the contents of the issue. Contents include the title and the stack trace. Matches must begin at alphanumeric tokens, i.e., 'util.Sorted' matches 'java.util.SortedSet' but not 'myutil.SortedArray'. The filter matches if all filter terms match. All non-alphanumeric characters are ignored for matching. Filtering is assumed to be prefix-search and order-independent unless phrases are surrounded by "". Any terms contained in quotes are searched using exact-match (given filter term "foo", we will not return "foobar"), and must appear in the order given exactly. To get order-dependence but prefix-search, use a * within the quotes ("abc foo*" will match "abc foobar", but not "foo abc" "abcd foobar", or "abc xyz foobar").

filter.issue.variantId.description: Optional. Only counts events for the given issue variant ID. This field matches [IssueVariant.id].

filter.issue.id.description: Optional. Only counts events in the given issue ID. This field matches [Issue.id].

readMask.description: Optional. The list of Event fields to include in the response. If omitted, the full event is returned.

filter.issue.content.description: Optional. A space separated list of filter terms matched against the contents of the issue. Contents include the title and the stack trace. Matches must begin at alphanumeric tokens, i.e., 'util.Sorted' matches 'java.util.SortedSet' but not 'myutil.SortedArray'. The filter matches if all filter terms match. All non-alphanumeric characters are ignored for matching. Filtering is assumed to be prefix-search and order-independent unless phrases are surrounded by "". Any terms contained in quotes are searched using exact-match (given filter term "foo", we will not return "foobar"), and must appear in the order given exactly. To get order-dependence but prefix-search, use a * within the quotes ("abc foo*" will match "abc foobar", but not "foo abc" "abcd foobar", or "abc xyz foobar").

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of events per page. If omitted, defaults to 10.

list.description: List the events for an issue matching filter criteria, sorted in descending order by timestamp.

names.description: Required. The resource names of the desired events. A maximum of 100 events can be retrieved in a batch. Format: "projects/{project}/apps/{app_id}/events/{event_id}". The app_id and event_id are required, but project may be "-" to conserve space in long URIs.

readMask.description: Optional. The list of Event fields to include in the response. If omitted, the full event is returned.

batchGet.description: Fetch a batch of up to 100 events by name.
